title: PMS user and role report
source_system: PMS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: One pharmacy user account, the owner's, holding the administrator role; named vendor support accounts created by the PMS vendor; the role catalog includes a pharmacist role and a separate permission to annotate or alter controlled substance prescriptions, and only the administrator role is assigned; no account exists for the relief pharmacist; no record of a user list review

title: PMS sign-in and MFA settings
source_system: PMS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: MFA is enforced for web sign-in from outside the store, with the owner's phone as the only registered second factor; the store's network is set as a vendor-defined trusted location, where sign-in accepts a password alone; the owner's account password was last changed in 2023

title: PMS audit trail and EPCS audit report screens
source_system: PMS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The PMS records sign-ins, record access, and an EPCS audit trail; it generates a daily EPCS internal audit report and keeps the last 90; each retained report is marked unopened; the sign-in report, which lists failed sign-ins, has no run on record

title: PMS vendor remote-support agent settings
source_system: Remote-support agent on the counter desktop (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: The PMS vendor's remote-support agent is installed on the counter desktop with unattended access turned on; a vendor session can start at any time without a prompt or acceptance at the desktop; the agent keeps a session history

title: PMS service agreement and EPCS onboarding emails
source_system: Signed agreements folder; email inbox (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: The 2021 service agreement covers the hosted PMS, its e-prescribing network and claims switch (reached under the vendor's subcontractor agreements), real-time NCPDP claims to PBMs, and vendor support through a remote-support agent; the 2021 onboarding emails confirm EPCS processing was turned on at go-live; no third-party EPCS audit or certification report, and no request for one, appears in the inbox or the agreements folder; vendor notices about the application go to the owner's email

title: PMS prescription and patient volume report, January to June 2026
source_system: PMS reporting (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 650 active patients and about 2,400 individual patient records since the pharmacy opened in 2021; about 1,750 prescriptions in the half year, about 14 per business day, Monday to Friday; about 15% controlled substances; about 40 compounded prescriptions a month

title: PMS claims and payer report, January to June 2026
source_system: PMS reporting (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 90% of prescriptions adjudicated in real time with PBMs through the claims switch, for Medicare Part D plans, Florida Medicaid, and commercial plans; about 10% paid in cash

title: PMS PDMP submission log
source_system: PMS reporting (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The PMS sends a controlled substance dispensing file to the Florida PDMP automatically each business night; the log lists one file after each business day

title: PMS prescriber and patient address reports
source_system: PMS reporting (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: About 10 prescriber offices send most prescriptions; about 30 patients have addresses in states other than Florida (seasonal residents)

title: PMS DUR alert settings
source_system: PMS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Rule-based DUR alerts are on for interaction, duplicate therapy, dose range, allergy, age, and pregnancy and lactation screening; the vendor's rule descriptions list age, sex, pregnancy and lactation flags, allergies, medication history, and dose as inputs; the pharmacist acknowledges each alert, and no alert fills or blocks a prescription on its own

title: PMS refill reminder and refill phone line settings
source_system: PMS admin settings (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: The refill reminder text template contains only the pharmacy name and the words that a prescription is ready, with no drug name; the refill phone line asks for the prescription number only

title: Email and file suite admin console review
source_system: Email and file suite admin console (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Business plan; MFA on for the owner's account since 2024, with the phone as second factor; the console's BAA page offers the vendor's BAA with the status not accepted; the inbox holds faxed prescriptions and refill requests delivered as PDF attachments by the cloud fax service; file storage holds the master formulation records and compounding logs as spreadsheets, with version history on; the sign-in history is kept and has no review on record

title: Cloud fax portal settings
source_system: Cloud fax portal (SYS-06)
what_it_shows: Password sign-in; MFA is supported and turned off; each incoming fax is kept in the portal and also sent as a PDF to the owner's inbox

title: Counter desktop settings and contents review
source_system: Counter desktop settings screens (SYS-03)
what_it_shows: One shared local account with automatic sign-in and administrator rights; screen lock off; full-disk encryption off; automatic OS updates on, with the update history current; built-in antivirus on, with real-time scanning and automatic updates; host firewall on; the CSOS certificate is in the browser certificate store of the shared account, protected by its own password; files include scanned paper prescriptions, daily controlled substance reports downloaded from the PMS, and a 2025 patient mailing-list export of about 2,100 patients (names, addresses, birth dates); the browser history includes the AI chatbot and personal sites; label printer and document scanner attached; the owner restarts it each Friday after closing

title: Laptop and phone settings review
source_system: Laptop and phone settings screens (SYS-04; SYS-05)
what_it_shows: Laptop: full-disk encryption on; automatic updates on; built-in antivirus on; screen lock after 5 minutes; used for the books, email, and PMS web access from home with MFA; the downloads folder holds PMS reports. Phone: passcode set, device encryption on, lock after 1 minute, automatic updates on, remote wipe not set up; holds the second factor for email and for PMS web access from outside the store

title: Router and Wi-Fi settings
source_system: ISP router admin app (SYS-07)
what_it_shows: One network name for the whole store; the connected-device list shows the counter desktop, the security camera recorder, and customer phones; the router firewall is on; the Wi-Fi password is the one printed at the counter

title: Store walk-through
source_system: Store (observation)
what_it_shows: Wi-Fi password printed on a sign at the front counter; prescription department behind the counter and closed to the public, with deliveries received at the counter; locked controlled substance cabinet; monitored burglar alarm panel; security camera and recorder; paper prescriptions filed in a locked cabinet; cross-cut shredder in the back office; the counter desktop screen faces the counter and shows an open PMS session while the owner works at the compounding bench; a card with the PMS password in the counter drawer; the previous counter desktop, replaced in 2024, stored in the back office with no wipe or disposal record; store practices are not written down

title: Alarm monitoring agreement and user code list
source_system: Alarm monitoring company portal
what_it_shows: Monitored burglar alarm for the store; the portal lists 2 user codes, one for the owner and one for the relief pharmacist

title: Business associate agreement inventory
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: Signed BAAs with the PMS vendor (2021), the cloud fax vendor, and the on-call IT consultant (signed 2026-07-31); none for the email and file suite vendor, whose BAA is offered in its admin console (EV-012), or for the AI chatbot vendor

title: Bank and card statements, 2025-08-01 to 2026-07-24
source_system: Business bank account and card statements
what_it_shows: Recurring payments to the PMS vendor, the email and file suite (business plan), the cloud fax vendor, the internet service provider, the alarm monitoring company, the phone carrier, the accounting SaaS, the accountant, the business owner's and professional liability insurers, and the card processor; drug purchases from the wholesaler; hourly payments to the IT consultant and day-rate payments to the relief pharmacist; no payment to an AI chatbot vendor; no payment for a standalone cyber insurance policy

title: Relief pharmacist agreement, invoices, and relief-day sign-ins
source_system: Signed agreements folder; email inbox (SYS-02); PMS sign-in history (SYS-01)
what_it_shows: Independent contractor agreement with a Florida-licensed relief pharmacist for relief days and the owner's vacations, working under the owner's direction and the pharmacy's procedures; invoices show about 2 business days a month; the agreement has no confidentiality or security clause; the relief pharmacist holds a store key and the alarm code; no record of a license verification is kept in the files; on the invoiced relief days the PMS sign-in history shows the owner's account signed in at the store

title: IT consultant invoices, 2021 to 2026
source_system: Email inbox (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: A 2021 invoice for setting up the store network; hourly invoices since then for device and network help on request; no recurring service or standing access is billed

title: Wholesaler portal account and CSOS order history
source_system: Wholesaler ordering portal
what_it_shows: Ordering portal for non-controlled stock; Schedule II orders placed electronically and signed with the owner's CSOS certificate; order confirmations are emailed to the owner; the portal holds no patient data

title: Card processor merchant agreement
source_system: Signed agreements folder
what_it_shows: The card processor supplies a standalone card terminal on its own cellular connection; card data does not pass through the store network or the PMS

title: DEA registration and CSOS certificate records
source_system: DEA registration portal; CSOS certificate emails (SYS-02)
what_it_shows: Retail pharmacy registration for Schedules II to V; one CSOS certificate, issued to the owner; no power of attorney for CSOS ordering on file for anyone else

title: Florida pharmacy permit and license records
source_system: Florida Board of Pharmacy license verification portal
what_it_shows: Community pharmacy permit active for the Florida storefront; the owner is listed as prescription department manager; the owner's pharmacist license is active; no sterile compounding permit

title: Payer enrollments and PBM network agreements
source_system: Signed agreements folder; Florida Medicaid provider portal
what_it_shows: Enrolled Florida Medicaid pharmacy provider; PBM network agreements for Medicare Part D and commercial plans; claims are submitted in real time through the PMS's claims switch; the permit, enrollments, and agreements describe a community pharmacy and list no substance use disorder diagnosis, treatment, or referral service

title: 2025 Schedule C (Form 1040)
source_system: Owner's tax files (prepared by the accountant)
what_it_shows: Gross receipts of about $180,000; no wages paid; contract labor paid to the relief pharmacist; the business is a sole proprietorship with no employees

title: Business owner's and professional liability policy declarations
source_system: Insurance agent portal
what_it_shows: Business owner's policy and pharmacist professional liability policy in force for 2026; neither declarations page lists a cyber endorsement or states whether business-interruption coverage applies to a computer system outage; the full policy forms were requested from the agent

title: Search of the owner's files for security documents
source_system: Counter desktop; laptop; file suite; inbox; paper files
what_it_shows: Found: the notice of privacy practices and a 2021 privacy policy template. Not found: a written security policy or procedure, written access rules, an account removal procedure, a risk analysis, an incident plan, an EPCS incident reporting procedure, a contact list, a downtime procedure or printed medication list, a contingency plan, a sanction rule, a Security Officer designation, a device list, a device disposal or re-use procedure or record, a lock and alarm repair log, a retention rule, an AI use rule, or a written transfer arrangement with another pharmacy

title: Continuing education and training records
source_system: Florida continuing education tracking account; owner's files
what_it_shows: The owner's continuing education for the current license cycle covers pharmacy practice topics; no HIPAA security course or security reminder subscription appears; no security training record exists for the relief pharmacist

title: AI chatbot account and conversation history
source_system: Consumer AI chatbot account (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: Free personal account, first used on 2026-03-02 from the counter desktop and the phone; the history covers drafts of patient counseling sheets, checks of compounding calculations and formulations, and drug information questions; the setting that lets the vendor use chats to improve its models is on; the owner states that some conversations included patient details, and the number was not established at intake

title: AI chatbot terms of use, as accepted
source_system: AI chatbot vendor website
what_it_shows: Click-through consumer terms; no BAA is offered on the free plan; conversations may be used to improve the vendor's models while the training setting is on

title: BIA self-review worksheet
source_system: Pharmacist-owner's written BIA worksheet, reviewed with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: For each of the five business functions, the owner's account of the systems and vendors used, the manual workaround, and the longest outage and data loss the function can tolerate; the owner is the only person who performs or authorizes each function; cash reserves cover about one month of drug purchases; daily wholesaler deliveries cover about 2 to 3 days of stock

title: Risk walk-through of the store systems
source_system: Walk-through of the counter desktop, PMS settings, store network, and SaaS accounts with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: Where PHI sits day to day (PMS, desktop files, inbox, file suite, chatbot history); the open PMS session while the owner works at the compounding bench; the CSOS key in the shared desktop account; customer Wi-Fi on the store network; the relief-day sign-in practice; the controlled substance stock and the desktop kept in the same store

title: Gap analysis self-review
source_system: Pharmacist-owner's written answers to the HIPAA and EPCS questions, checked on screen with the IT consultant
what_it_shows: Incidents would be handled as they arise; the owner did not know the one-business-day DEA report for EPCS security incidents or the 24-hour CSOS compromise report; checks for duplicate electronic prescriptions are made case by case at the counter, with no written step for a PMS outage; there is no procedure to stop EPCS processing after a vendor notice; there is no procedure to end a user's access; the relief pharmacist works alone on relief days; the owner checked the relief pharmacist's Florida license online in 2025 and kept no record; nothing is written about store access in an emergency; lock and alarm repairs are not recorded; no rule exists for copying data before a device is moved or replaced; contingency arrangements have never been tested; security documents are kept in the file suite and the relief pharmacist has no copy

title: PMS vendor SOC 2 Type 2 report
source_system: PMS vendor (provided under a nondisclosure agreement)
what_it_shows: Type 2 report on the Security and Availability categories for 2025-04-01 to 2026-03-31, unqualified opinion; one exception: for 2 of 40 sampled departed vendor staff, access was removed later than the vendor's 1-business-day standard (remediated); the system description states RPO 1 hour and RTO 12 hours, an annual failover test, and backups encrypted and kept in a separate region; TLS on all services and encryption at rest; lists complementary user entity controls; the e-prescribing network, the claims switch, and the hosting provider are carved out; a bridge letter was requested on 2026-08-05

title: EPCS certification report
source_system: PMS vendor (obtained on request)
what_it_shows: Issued 2025-11-14 by a DEA-approved certification organization; finds the PMS accurately and consistently imports, stores, and displays the required prescription information, the indication of signing, and refills, with no limitation; the last intermediary digitally signs each record before transmission; the PMS enforces role-based access with a separate annotation permission, protects audit records from deletion and modification, and backs up controlled substance records daily; next report due by 2027-11-14; read by the owner for the first time on 2026-08-05

title: BAA terms review
source_system: Signed agreements folder (EV-019)
what_it_shows: The PMS vendor BAA (2021) contains the terms listed in 45 CFR 164.314(a)(2)(i) and requires its subcontractors to agree to the same terms; it requires breach notice within 30 days and reports other security incidents only on request; the cloud fax BAA says nothing about subcontractors

title: AI use review: chatbot conversation history
source_system: Consumer AI chatbot account (SYS-08)
what_it_shows: About 60 conversations from 2026-03-02 to 2026-08-07: about 35 drafting counseling sheets, about 15 checking compounding calculations or formulations, about 10 drug information questions; patient details (names or initials, ages, drugs, doses; allergies in 2) appear in 6 conversations, each about one patient; in one conversation the chatbot converted a percentage strength to milligrams incorrectly, and the owner caught it against the master formulation record; the training setting was on until it was turned off on 2026-08-12

title: Control assessment: Remote access test
source_system: Remote-support agent settings and session history; PMS remote access settings; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The remote-support agent was configured for unattended access at any time; its session history shows 9 vendor sessions in the past 12 months, none watched; no written usage rules or guidance for vendor remote support or PMS access from home; both remote access types were set up by the owner before use; the agent was switched to attended mode during the test

title: Control assessment: EPCS audit report review
source_system: PMS daily EPCS audit reports (90 retained); PMS sign-in report; email sign-in history; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The daily EPCS audit reports and the sign-in reports had never been opened; the first review of the 90 retained reports found 3 failed sign-ins, all explained by the owner, and no alteration or access-control events; no process exists to act on or report review results, or to increase review after an incident or vendor notice

title: Control assessment: Backup review and record retrieval test
source_system: PMS vendor SOC 2 and EPCS certification reports; file suite settings; record retrieval test
what_it_shows: The PMS vendor backs up the system with an RPO of 1 hour and backs up controlled substance records daily, encrypted and in a separate region (SOC 2 and EPCS certification reports, no exceptions in backup controls); controlled substance records were retrieved intact by patient, prescriber, drug, and date; master formulation records, compounding logs, and the new security documents exist only in the file suite, where version history is the only copy

title: Control assessment: Account and EPCS record test
source_system: PMS user list; desktop accounts; sample of 10 EPCS dispensing records from the last 12 months; relief schedule; relief pharmacist (by phone)
what_it_shows: One PMS pharmacy account shared by the owner and the relief pharmacist, and one shared automatic sign-in desktop account; 2 of the 10 sampled EPCS dispensing records were filled on relief days and name the owner as the dispensing pharmacist; annotations in the sample were made in the PMS annotation fields; the relief pharmacist confirmed by phone that relief-day sign-in uses the owner's account; the PMS password card in the counter drawer was destroyed and the password changed during the session

title: Control assessment: PMS administrator MFA sign-in test
source_system: PMS security settings; sign-in tests from the counter desktop and from the laptop over the phone hotspot
what_it_shows: Administrator sign-in from the laptop outside the store network required the second factor; sign-in from the counter desktop accepted the password alone (vendor trusted-location setting)

title: Control assessment: Incident reporting self-review
source_system: Contact lists; BAAs (reporting clauses); relief pharmacist agreement; owner self-review
what_it_shows: No reporting time is set; the relief pharmacist has no duty to report incidents to the owner; there is no list of whom to notify (PMS vendor, DEA, CSOS certificate authority, counsel, HHS, Florida)

title: Control assessment: Risk analysis review
source_system: P01 risk register; P05 BIA; owner self-review
what_it_shows: The 2026 risk analysis identifies 15 threat events with sources and vulnerabilities, including EPCS and CSOS ones; it rates likelihood and impact with Tables G-5 and I-2, includes harm to patients, takes its business view from the BIA, and is documented; no review frequency or update trigger was defined at the time of assessment

title: Control assessment: Vendor and BAA review
source_system: BAA folder; vendor list; PMS vendor SOC 2 and EPCS certification reports; AI chatbot account
what_it_shows: The email and file suite holds faxed prescriptions with its BAA not accepted; patient details were pasted into an AI chatbot with no BAA; no vendor list, required vendor safeguards, or oversight steps are documented; PMS customer responsibilities are listed in the SOC 2 report's complementary user entity controls and the vendor support role in the PMS contract; the vendor reports were read for the first time on 2026-08-05; no ongoing monitoring of the PMS, fax, or email vendors

title: Control assessment: Encryption status check
source_system: Encryption status of the desktop, laptop, and phone; desktop file review; PMS vendor SOC 2 report
what_it_shows: Desktop full-disk encryption off; the desktop holds scanned prescriptions, daily controlled substance reports, and a 2025 mailing-list export of about 2,100 patients; laptop and phone encrypted; PMS data encrypted by the vendor

title: Control assessment: Network scan and router review
source_system: Router settings; network scan by the IT consultant; network walk-through
what_it_shows: The scan found the desktop, the camera recorder, and customer Wi-Fi clients on one network and no inbound ports open on the router; the router firewall blocks unsolicited inbound connections; nothing monitors traffic at the router or between devices, and the router logs have never been reviewed; the ISP router is the only external connection
